papers.title: Butcher series for Hamiltonian Poisson integrators through symplectic groupoids
papers.abstract: We exhibit a new pre-Lie algebra in the framework of symplectic groupoids and, in turn, use Butcher trees to compute the Taylor series of a solution of a Hamilton-Jacobi equation on any symplectic groupoid $\mathcal{G} \rightrightarrows M.$ The impact of this new algebraic approach is twofold. On the geometric side, it yields algebraic operations to approximate Lagrangian bisections of $\mathcal{G}$ using the Butcher-Connes-Kreimer Hopf algebra and, in turn, aims at a better understanding of the group of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of $M.$ On the computational side, we define a new class of Poisson integrators for Hamiltonian dynamics on Poisson manifolds.

papers.title: Open WDVV equations for non-commutative families of bounding cochains
papers.abstract: We derive the noncommutative open WDVV equations for the open Gromov-Witten superpotential introduced in joint work of the author and Solomon, extending the Solomon-Tukachinsky equations to noncommutative differential graded algebras. The resulting recursive formulas facilitate the computation of open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints for even-dimensional Lagrangians. We apply the open WDVV equations to compute all open Gromov-Witten invariants for the real loci of even-dimensional complex quadrics of dimension greater than two. These computations show that open Gromov-Witten invariants with multiple boundary point constraints can be nontrivial in arbitrary dimensions. We also construct a character for a natural subalgebra of big quantum cohomology associated to a Lagrangian endowed with a point-like bounding cochain. The character is in the spirit of the Kodaira-Spencer map of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono. Applying the character construction to the even-dimensional quadric illustrates how point-like bounding cochains refine the information about closed quantum cohomology obtained from weak bounding cochains of Floer theory. Open Gromov-Witten invariants with three boundary point constraints determine the two extensions of the character from the subalgebra to big quantum cohomology.

papers.title: Holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphism groups via the Symplectic Density Property
papers.abstract: We show that the cotangent bundle of a holomorphically flexible Stein manifold has the symplectic density property. As application we deduce holomorphic approximation for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms of real cotangent bundles by complex symplectic automorphisms of the complexified cotangent bundles, which preserve the real bundle, in the Carleman sense, i.e. in the Whitney topology.

papers.title: On some rigidity results for high-dimensional confoliations
papers.abstract: The main result is an obstruction to the presence of contact regions for c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension. As a first application, we prove a 5-dimensional analogue (under stronger assumptions) of a Reeb stability theorem for confoliations in dimension 3 due to Eliashberg and Thurston. Refining work of the first author with Cardona, we further give two new notions of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations in any odd ambient dimension generalizing the 3-dimensional notion of Eliashberg-Thurston. As a second application of our main theorem, we then give an example, in any ambient odd dimension, of a c-symplectic (and in fact strong symplectic) foliation that cannot be contact approximated, in either of these two senses. This relies on the property, of independent interest, that contact structures approximating (in these senses) a weakly c-symplectic confoliation are also weakly fillable. The proofs of all these statements rely on pseudo-holomorphic curve theory. Lastly, we describe several natural classes of examples of these types of contact approximations of c-symplectic confoliations.

papers.title: Canonical coordinates for moduli spaces of rank two irregular connections on curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a geometric counterpart of the cyclic vector which allow us to put a rank 2 meromorphic connection on a curve into a ``companion'' normal form. This allow us to naturally identify an open set of the moduli space of $\mathrm{GL}_2$-connections (with fixed generic spectral data, i.e. unramified, non resonant) with some Hilbert scheme of points on the twisted cotangent bundle of the curve. We prove that this map is symplectic, therefore providing Darboux (or canonical) coordinates on the moduli space, i.e. separation of variables. On the other hand, for $\mathrm{SL}_2$-connections, we give an explicit formula for the symplectic structure for a birational model given by Matsumoto. We finally detail the case of an elliptic curve with a divisor of degree $2$.

papers.title: Unramified Gromov-Witten and Gopakumar-Vafa invariants
papers.abstract: Kim, Kresch, and Oh defined unramified Gromov-Witten invariants. For threefolds, Pandharipande conjectured that these invariants are equal to the Gopakumar-Vafa (BPS) invariants for Fano and primitive Calabi-Yau curve classes. We prove the conjecture using a wall-crossing method developed here. As a result, we obtain an algebro-geometric construction of Gopakumar-Vafa invariants in these cases.

papers.title: On the Finiteness of Anosov flows on $3$-manifolds via Contact Geometry
papers.abstract: In dimension 3, following Eliashberg-Thurston and Mitsumatsu, one can associate a transverse pair of oppositely oriented contact structures to any Anosov flow. We show that when the ambient manifold is hyperbolic, the isotopy classes of these contact structures completely determine the flow up to isotopy orbit equivalence. This then implies that on any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold, the number of Anosov flows modulo isotopy orbit equivalence is finite. This approach also yields an explicit bound on the number of orbit equivalence classes of Anosov flows in terms of the number of universally tight contact structures. In addition, we show finiteness of pseudo-Anosov flows for which the complement of the singular orbits is atoroidal and, in the non- hyperbolic case, we obtain a control on the dynamics of Anosov flows on the hyperbolic pieces of the JSJ-decomposition.

papers.title: Removal of singularities in Morse-Bott symplectizations
papers.abstract: Hofer-Wysocki-Zehnder and Bourgeois proved that a finite energy punctured pseudoholomorphic curve in the symplectization of a Morse-Bott contact manifold either has a removable singularity or asymptotes to a Reeb orbit. We give an alternate proof of this result.

papers.title: Transfer maps in symplectic cohomology for convex symplectic domains
papers.abstract: We construct transfer maps in symplectic cohomology for convex symplectic domains, assuming that the complement of a subdomain is exact. The construction uses an action filtration by Reeb periods, inspired by that of McLean--Ritter. The transfer maps yield the invariance of symplectic cohomology under subcritical handle attachment to convex symplectic domains. As an application, we obtain infinitely many exotic convex symplectic structures on certain domains via McLean's exotic Stein balls.
